answer: Require each agent identity to be backed by a stake bonded to one verified controller, with slashing on proven duplicate operation: creating ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand bonds, while one honest agent pays once. A stake registry acts as a ridge between cheap talk and costly commitment — crossing it is free to read but expensive to fake. Like a sonnet, the rule is short and fixed, so peers can check it mechanically; like ferrous metal under a magnet, duplicate identities cluster visibly when their bonds trace to the same controller, and the cluster can be slashed as one.
